verses.text: When Jesus had finished teaching all these things, he said to his disciples,
“You know the Passover is in two days, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, scribes, and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, Caiaphas.
They plotted to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
“Not during the festival,” they said, “or the people might riot.”
While Jesus was in Bethany, at the home of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume. As he was reclining at the table, she poured it on his head.
When the disciples saw it, they were upset. “Why waste it like that?” they asked.
“It could have been sold for a lot and the money given to the poor.”
Jesus knew what they were saying and told them, “Why are you giving this woman a hard time? She has done something beautiful for me.
“You will always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me.
“By pouring this perfume on my body, she has prepared me for burial.
“I tell you the truth: wherever this Good News is announced throughout the world, people will also tell what she did, in memory of her.”
Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and asked, “What will you give me if I hand him over to you?” They counted out thirty pieces of silver for him.
From then on, Judas looked for a chance to betray Jesus.
On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you?”
He said, “Go into the city and find a certain person. Tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
The disciples did what Jesus told them and got the Passover ready.
When evening came, Jesus was reclining at the table with the Twelve.
As they ate, he said, “I tell you the truth: one of you will betray me.”
They were deeply upset, and each one began asking him, “Surely you don’t mean me, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand into the dish with me is the one who will betray me.
“The Son of Man will go just as Scripture says about him. But how terrible for the one who betrays the Son of Man! It would have been better for that person never to have been born.”
Judas, the one who was betraying him, asked, “Surely you don’t mean me, Rabbi?” Jesus replied, “You said it.”
While they were eating, Jesus took some bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to the disciples. “Take it and eat,” he said. “This is my body.”
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them. “All of you, drink from it,
“because this is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
“I tell you, I will not drink this fruit of the vine again until the day I drink it new with you in my Father’s Kingdom.”
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus told them, “Tonight you will all stumble because of me, as Scripture says: ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will scatter.’
“But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter replied, “Even if everyone else stumbles because of you, I never will.”
Jesus told him, “I tell you the truth: before the rooster crows tonight, you will deny me three times.”
Peter said, “Even if I have to die with you, I will never deny you.” All the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane. He told his disciples, “Sit here while I go over there to pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him. He began to feel deep sorrow and distress.
Then Jesus said to them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow, close to death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”
He went a little farther, fell facedown, and prayed: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Still, let what you want happen, not what I want.”
He returned to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Couldn’t you stay awake with me for even one hour?
“Stay alert and pray so you don’t give in to temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
He went away a second time and prayed, “My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, then let your will be done.”
He came back and found them sleeping again, because their eyes were heavy.
So he left them, went away once more, and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
Then he returned to the disciples and said, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.
“Get up; let’s go. Look, the one betraying me is here.”
While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived. A large crowd came with him, carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.
The betrayer had arranged a signal with them: “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him.”
Judas went straight to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” Then he kissed him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then the crowd came forward, grabbed Jesus, and arrested him.
One of the people with Jesus reached for his sword, drew it, and struck the high priest’s servant, cutting off his ear.
Jesus told him, “Put your sword away. Everyone who takes up the sword will die by the sword.
“Don’t you think I could ask my Father, and he would send more than twelve legions of angels right now?
“But then how would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say this must happen?”
At that moment Jesus said to the crowd, “Did you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me like I’m a robber? Every day I sat teaching in the temple, and you didn’t arrest me.
“But all this has happened so the words of the prophets in Scripture would be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and ran away.
The people who arrested Jesus took him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Peter followed him from a distance to the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
The chief priests, elders, and whole council looked for false testimony against Jesus so they could put him to death.
Many false witnesses came forward, but they found no case. At last two witnesses came forward
and said, “This man claimed, ‘I can destroy God’s temple and rebuild it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and asked Jesus, “Aren’t you going to answer? What do you say about these charges?”
But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said to him, “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus answered, “You have said it. But I tell you this: from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on heaven’s clouds.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has spoken blasphemy! Why do we need more witnesses? You just heard it.
“What’s your verdict?” They answered, “He deserves death!”
Then they spat in his face and punched him. Others slapped him
and said, “Prophesy to us, Christ! Who hit you?”
Meanwhile Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, “You were with Jesus the Galilean too.”
But he denied it in front of everyone: “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
When he went out to the entrance, another person saw him and told the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth.”
Again Peter denied it, this time with an oath: “I don’t know the man.”
A little later, those standing nearby came to Peter and said, “You must be one of them. Your accent gives you away.”
Then he began to curse and swear, “I don’t know the man!” At once a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: “Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
